gloss: to pile up, to stack, to repeat

definitions.explanation: To place things one on top of another.
To do something repeatedly over time.

examples.japanese: ⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{重|かさ}ねる。
⟦{布|ぬの}→布：01489_nuno⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{二枚|にまい}{重|かさ}ねる。
examples.english: To layer two pieces of cloth.

examples.english: After repeated discussions, they finally reached an agreement.

notes:
{重|かさ}ねる means to pile up or stack (literally), and to repeat or accumulate (figuratively).

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Pair: {重|かさ}なる (intransitive, "to pile up")

ASPECT (ている):
{重|かさ}ねている indicates an ongoing state of having been stacked, or continued repetition.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {皿|さら}を{重|かさ}ねる: to stack plates
- {努力|どりょく}を{重|かさ}ねる: to make repeated efforts
- {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねる: to grow older (lit. pile up years)
- {経験|けいけん}を{重|かさ}ねる: to accumulate experience
- {話|はな}し{合|あ}いを{重|かさ}ねる: to have repeated discussions

The figurative sense emphasizes gradual accumulation over time.
